question: Who wrote the book 'Pancha Siddhantika' during the Gupta period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Varahamihira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Varahamihira** was a renowned Indian astronomer, mathematician, and astrologer during the **Gupta period**.
 
• He is the author of the famous work **'Pancha Siddhantika'**, which means "Five Treatises."
 
• The **'Pancha Siddhantika'** is a significant astronomical text that compiles and synthesizes knowledge from five earlier astronomical schools or treatises:
 
 
• **Surya Siddhanta**
 
• **Paulisa Siddhanta**
 
• **Vasistha Siddhanta**
 
• **Romaka Siddhanta**
 
• **Paitamaha Siddhanta**
 
 
 
• The book provides insights into the **astronomical calculations** of the time and highlights advancements in **Indian astronomy**.
 
• It also includes discussions on the motion of planets, eclipses, and other celestial phenomena.
 
• **Varahamihira** was a key figure in the **Gupta Golden Age**, a period renowned for its advancements in art, science, and literature.
 
• His contributions had a significant influence on both **Indian and Islamic astronomy** in later centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amarasimha**__

 __
 
• **Amarasimha** was a scholar and lexicographer in the court of **Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II.**
 
• He is famous for writing the **'Amarakosha'**, an ancient Sanskrit thesaurus.
 
• The **'Amarakosha'** is one of the earliest and most authoritative lexicons in Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Vararuchi**__
 __
 
• **Vararuchi** was an ancient Indian scholar associated with **linguistics** and **grammar.**
 
• He is believed to have contributed to the **Katyayana school of Sanskrit grammar.**
 
• Some sources also associate him with the **Paninian grammar tradition.**
 
 
 
• **Kshapanaka**__
 
 
• **Kshapanaka** was one of the **'Navaratnas'** (Nine Gems) in the court of **Vikramaditya.**
 
• He is primarily known as a **poet and scholar**, but not for any significant contributions to astronomy.
